trigger: Initialize an unconfigured project; exercise Herdr, Orca, CLI and none, including each project Skill target for Herdr/Orca
expected: Offers four choices; external defaults are preferred with lead fallback, none persists lead, and only Herdr/Orca ask for a project Skill directory. Saves the relative guide and reuses the complete local Skill. If missing, directs the user to SKILLS-HUB in speculo init; never downloads GitHub main or starts services.

trigger: Repeat initialization with saved lead or external preferences; then explicitly change the default mode
expected: Displays and reuses valid preferences without asking again. Explicit changes replace defaults while preserving Work/stage rules and old third-party files; obsolete tool/model/guide fields are not carried into another mode. A saved preference alone does not authorize reinstalling a missing Skill.

trigger: Read-only initialization, plan-only initialization, unanswered/cancelled selection, or a normal Work without coordination configuration
expected: Does not install Skills, save defaults, start services or create business state; an unanswered choice is not treated as consent to persist lead. A normal Work uses its current host without starting the initialization questionnaire.

trigger: Choose Herdr/Orca but its project Skill is missing, or a previous CLI installation was interrupted
expected: Keeps the saved preference and target, reports not installed and continues independent initialization with lead fallback. Directs installation and transaction recovery to the Speculo CLI with its bundled automation/herdr or automation/orca package; never writes CLI metadata or installs from GitHub main.

trigger: Initialization encounters invalid configuration, configuration drift, a linked install path, an invalid same-name Skill or two legacy Skill candidates without a saved guide
expected: Preserves original files and stops only affected writes; invalid configuration does not trigger dependent installation. Ambiguous directories require a user choice; valid explicit guide paths are honored and no global Skill directory is substituted.

trigger: Execute an authorized task with preferred Herdr, Orca or CLI plus lead fallback when its Skill, CLI, service, login or required environment is unavailable before dispatch
expected: Reports the unavailable capability and continues with the current agent without repeating the choice, changing saved preferences or installing/starting a service. Independent review still requires an eligible reviewer; an implementer cannot approve their own work.

trigger: A required tool or stage overrides an optional project default, or an external dispatch loses its response while the worker may still be writing
expected: Does not inherit lower-priority fallback for a forced choice. For uncertain dispatch, recovers the original task and verifies effects and stopped writers before continuing unfinished work; a service error never justifies duplicate execution.

trigger: explicit source intake request
expected: freezes a source-backed change; clear local requests need no triage

trigger: reproducible bug
expected: requires red evidence before repair

trigger: clear external behavior
expected: produces a ready specification

trigger: ready specification
expected: produces decision-complete tickets

trigger: implementation ticket
expected: runs test-first verification

trigger: fixed diff
expected: records immutable review input

trigger: failed implementation
expected: resumes from checkpoint

trigger: completed change
expected: archives only after evidence

trigger: new learning goal
expected: creates an adaptive course plan

trigger: course plan ready
expected: writes a complete lesson

trigger: user explicitly requests homework
expected: creates explicit homework; lesson completion alone does not trigger it

trigger: delayed review requested
expected: requires real retention evidence

trigger: user selects topic changes
expected: creates provenance-backed synthesis

trigger: legacy v1 state
expected: blocks without migration

trigger: explicit deployment planning request
expected: identifies registered resource target and scope

trigger: registered host and deployment facts ready
expected: creates digest-bound plan

trigger: target mutation inside or outside a frozen task
expected: requires exact plan approval or the existing bounded task authorization; a document saying approved is not authorization

trigger: approved plan
expected: records typed operations

trigger: failed gate
expected: stops forward mutation and preserves recovery

trigger: verified resource run
expected: retains immutable Run/Release evidence; does not create a change archive

trigger: complex choice
expected: freezes two-sided dossier

trigger: strategy consultation
expected: uses methodology as a decision lens

trigger: context threshold reached
expected: writes recoverable checkpoint

trigger: model session starts
expected: performs capability handshake

trigger: Have an offline-sync requirement and want to understand reference projects before design
expected: Explains the references, data flow and applicability with sources; creates and completes a learning-only change after delivery; does not activate implementation.

trigger: Ask how a local module works without selecting a change
expected: Explains the relevant code and distinguishes static reading from executed tests; creates a learning change instead of attaching to another active change.

trigger: Ask about an explicitly selected development change
expected: Appends sourced Markdown/ASCII lessons and index rows to that change; preserves development scope, acceptance, owner and Outcome.

trigger: Ask to understand an external project or article with no development task
expected: Explains features, implementation ideas and author claims from accessible sources; persists the learning round without inventing a Spec, Ticket or implementation authorization.

trigger: The article or repository needed for a learning question cannot be accessed
expected: Reports the missing source and pauses dependent conclusions; continues supported parts, does not fabricate content or mark the blocked learning round completed.

trigger: Continue questions after delivery or resume after a lesson write succeeded but index update failed
expected: Reuses the selected change, preserves Outcome and old lessons, and repairs the original missing index row before allocating another number.

trigger: Select an archived change as the subject of a learning request
expected: Reads the archive without modification and saves sourced lessons in a new learning change; does not reopen, move or append to the archived object.

trigger: User assigns Codex planning, Grok tickets/map, a Learning explanation, and PI review
expected: Uses actual tool/model choices and dependency inputs; workers write assigned artifacts, Lead verifies via original owners. No mandatory Goal/Ticket or SpecDev installation for generic coordination.

trigger: Install only core, Learning or OPS; dispatch without a SpecDev change
expected: The public initialization command and shared v2 validator resolve without SpecDev files; no fake change or business state; global sessions retain their original root.

trigger: Ordinary completion, status request or plan-only handoff; later an explicit handoff request
expected: No handoff write until explicit execution request; completion does not auto-spawn a handoff worker. Explicit handoff can summarize unfinished work.

trigger: Explicit handoff twice after progress and a user addition
expected: Rereads actual artifacts and prior handoff.md, preserves valid context and user additions, revises obsolete conclusions with evidence; does not update business completion or approvals.

trigger: Handoff spans several changes, OPS resources, or no change
expected: Updates writable changes separately; writes one non-overwriting whole-session report with pointers and per-object results; no invented business objects.

trigger: An archived object, drift, a lock or one failed write occurs during multi-object handoff
expected: Archives and conflicting originals remain unchanged; successful independent writes retained; per-object report shows failures and original recovery routes; retries reread actual files, never replay unknown effects.
